problem:
Determine the **largest** interval on which the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2x+4}$ is concave up.

The largest interval where $f(x)$ is concave up is
$(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
First, we notice that the domain of the function is $x\ne -2.$

A function $f(x)$ is concave up on an interval $(a,b)$ if ${f}^{″}(x)>0$ for all $x\in (a,b).$

First, let's calculate the second derivative of $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2x+4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{(2x)(2x+4)-2{x}^{2}}{(2x+4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x(x+4)}{(2x+4)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+8x}{(2x+4)^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =\frac{(4x+8)(2x+4)^{2}-4(2{x}^{2}+8x)(2x+4)}{(2x+4)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{8(x+2)^{2}-8{x}^{2}-32x}{(2x+4)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{8{x}^{2}+32x+32-8{x}^{2}-32x}{(2x+4)^{3}} \\  & =\frac{4}{(x+2)^{3}} \\  & =4(x+2)^{-3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find where the function is concave up, we solve the inequality ${f}^{″}(x)>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x+2)^{-3} & >0 \\ (x+2)^{-3} & >0 \\ x+2 & >0 \\ x & >-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ is concave up on $(\,-2,\infty \,).$
